source_refs.note: Exercise 3.4, Question 7: Exercise 3.4, book page 94: Q1-Q15 (integration by partial fractions); answers book pages 301-302

blocks.explanation:
The linear factor \(x + 2\) is repeated three times: Case-II.
A repeated factor \((x + 2)^3\) needs three fractions, with powers 1, 2 and 3.
Plan: find \(C\) by putting \(x = -2\), then \(A\) and \(B\) by comparing coefficients; integrate with the power rule.
steps:
Given: \(\int \frac{x^2 - 3}{(x + 2)^3}\,dx\).
To find: the integral.
Method: partial fractions, Case-II (repeated linear factor). The fraction is proper: degree 2 < degree 3.

Write the partial fractions
\[\dfrac{x^2 - 3}{(x + 2)^3} = \dfrac{A}{x + 2} + \dfrac{B}{(x + 2)^2} + \dfrac{C}{(x + 2)^3}\]
\[x^2 - 3 = A(x + 2)^2 + B(x + 2) + C \quad (1)\]
Why: \((x + 2)^3\) gives one fraction for each power up to 3.

Put \(x = -2\) in (1)
\[4 - 3 = C\]
\[C = 1\]
Why: \(x + 2 = 0\) removes the \(A\) and \(B\) terms.

Compare coefficients in (1)
\[x^2:\ 1 = A\]
\[x:\ 0 = 4A + B,\ B = -4\]
Why: \(A(x + 2)^2 = A(x^2 + 4x + 4)\). Only one root exists, so the other constants come from comparing coefficients.

Check (constant term of (1))
\[4A + 2B + C = 4 - 8 + 1 = -3 \;\checkmark\]
Why: The constant term on the left of (1) is \(-3\); the values of \(A\), \(B\), \(C\) give the same.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: In the answers at the end of the book (page 301), the answers of Exercise 3.4 are printed under the wrong heading "Exercise 3.6". The answer of this question is item (vii) of that block: \(\ln|x + 2| + \frac{4}{x + 2} - \frac{1}{2(x + 2)^2} + c\). That answer is correct. The block headed "Exercise 3.4" (page 301) belongs to a different exercise.
